Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II in scope for production vendors. If you have Type I only or "in progress" status, please give expected completion date and whether you can share interim evidence (SOC 2 Type I report, control matrix).

- GDPR / HIPAA: GDPR applies for EU data; HIPAA applies only to PHI workloads. At a minimum, we need assurance on data residency controls, processing agreements (DPA), and for HIPAA a signed BAA before onboarding any PHI.

- Deletion SLA: Our legal team prefers deletion of customer data (primary and backups) within 30 days of request, with the exception of legal hold. Can you confirm Redwood’s default for backups and whether backups are retained longer than 30 days? Also please confirm what is included in "customer data" vs operational logs/metrics.

- Logs: We also typically ask for 365-day log retention for audit purposes, but this is negotiable for enterprise plans. Can you confirm your default and options for extending retention?

I’ve attached the questionnaire (we’ll send the completed copy back after our internal review). Happy to set a technical meeting with Neha — can do Monday or Tuesday morning PT.

Hi Jordan — looping in from Security to address the specifics you raised. Short answers up front, followed by a few notes and links to policy docs.

SOC 2
- Current status: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I (security) in 2026. We have Type II in progress and expect Type II completion by 2027-09 (Q3 2027).
- Interim evidence: We can share the Type I report, the control matrix, and our SOC 2 roadmap (internal schedule + gaps) under an NDA.

GDPR / HIPAA
- GDPR: We support GDPR requirements via our DPA (encryption at rest/in transit, subprocessor list, data processing terms). We can support EU data residency via regional deployments and routing policies; please indicate if you require data to stay in EU.
- HIPAA: We can enter a BAA for PHI use cases; product-level controls include encryption, access controls, and audit logging. For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment depending on your risk tolerance.

Data deletion / backups
- Primary data: On deletion request we remove customer data from active stores immediately; irreversible deletion from active storage is completed within 30 days in our standard offering.
- Backups: Backups are rotated and retained for up to 90 days in our standard configuration to support disaster recovery. Backups may persist as encrypted snapshots; deletion from backup snapshots follows the rotation window (up to 90 days).
- Legal hold: Legal holds will pause deletion per contract (standard practice).

Logs and audit retention
- Default: Application & audit logs retention is 180 days by default for hosted customers.
- Extended retention: We can support 365-day retention for logs/audit trails as a contract add-on for enterprise deals (pricing and storage terms apply).

Notes & next steps
- We can accept Amaya’s questionnaire; please return the filled copy and we’ll provide the supporting artifacts (Type I report, DPA, encryption & key mgmt docs, penetration test summary).
- If you require deletion-from-backups within 30 days as a hard SLA, we should document that as a special contract term (technical/operational implications: reduced DR window).
- For PHI use, we recommend Dedicated/Private deployment and a BAA; Neha (security) can join a short technical call to discuss.

I’m attaching our data retention SLA doc for reference (Redwood_Data_Retention_SLA.pdf). Happy to jump on a call Monday 10am PT — Marissa, Jordan, does that work?

Regards,
